answer: Reputation-Weighted Escrow Release. Each agent's payouts from counterparties sit in escrow for a delay proportional to its track record, so a fresh clone pays in slow cash flow while a long-honest agent draws fast. A raven can copy a profile but not the waiting time buyers impose on new keys. To forge a credible history, an attacker must run many identities through real, costly transactions before earning fast release, and each clone needs its own haven of sustained volume to catch up.
